hearing.readScope: Actual complete benefits/limitations section read, including communication, background sound, adjustment and cost.
hearing.role: Selected device benefits and limits only; US adult OTC eligibility is not transferred to Ontario children. No fitting, diagnosis or product recommendation.

firefly.readScope: Actual firefly and visitor-impact main text read; updated October 14, 2026. No media inspected.
firefly.role: Specific Great Smoky Mountains firefly communication/light-disturbance case, not every insect or all lighting.

ocean-noise.readScope: Actual introduction, importance of sound, large-vessel source paragraph, masking/behaviour and complexity/reduction text read. No figures or PDF inspected.
ocean-noise.role: Ship propeller sound can overlap important signals; response depends on species, activity and exposure. No universal harm rate or guaranteed local recovery.

accessible-signal.sourceSummary: Toronto describes paired visual, audible and vibrating pedestrian signals with adjustable sound and installation/maintenance constraints.
accessible-signal.attributionLimits: Original classroom analysis of an attributed municipal system, not a road-crossing lesson or testimony from all users.
accessible-signal.question: Compare a supplied original text description of a visual-only crossing signal with the City-described combined signal. Explain who may benefit, how the signal communicates timing/direction, and why maintenance, clear meaning and background conditions matter. Rank function/accessibility, safety, cost, energy/material use and appearance for this particular brief, explaining the trade-off.
accessible-signal.expectedEvidence: Explain an accessibility benefit without treating every user as identical. Visual, audible and tactile routes can complement one another; producing a louder noise alone does not guarantee an unambiguous message. Relate an actual design feature to the named need, give a limitation and justify priorities.
accessible-signal.nearMiss: Says brighter/louder is always better, all users can rely on one channel, or the device itself guarantees safe crossing.
accessible-signal.changedCase: An original fictional brief changes the setting to a quiet residential evening: reconsider an always-loud signal versus adjustment and vibration without assuming accessibility can simply be removed.

hearing-aid.sourceSummary: FDA lists possible communication benefits alongside background-noise, adjustment and cost limitations.
hearing-aid.attributionLimits: Information task only; neither a promise of restored typical hearing nor a clinical assessment.
hearing-aid.question: Use the selected source summaries to compare a conversation with and without an appropriately fitted hearing aid for a fictional user. Explain a possible benefit in family/group communication and two limitations; contrast this with a signal that helps communicate outside the ear.
hearing-aid.expectedEvidence: Sound amplification may support communication but does not restore all hearing; unwanted background sound, adjustment and cost can matter. Compare whose needs and circumstances are met, with evidence rather than a cure claim.
hearing-aid.nearMiss: Says every hearing aid removes background sound completely or that difficulty means the user did not try hard enough.
hearing-aid.changedCase: In a noisier fictional room, identify what additional information would be needed before judging success; do not prescribe settings or equipment.

firefly-light.sourceSummary: At this named park, artificial visitor lighting can disrupt synchronous firefly communication; the provider limits disruptive visitor behaviour.
firefly-light.attributionLimits: Specific attributed case; no inference that all insect decline has one cause or that all lights must be removed. Fictional perspectives below are original assessment roles.
firefly-light.question: Original brief: a park organiser wants a well-lit event, a visitor wants a usable route and a conservation worker wants firefly signalling protected. Use the actual park account to assess a proposed continuously bright display beside the firefly area. Compare limiting unnecessary light, directed lighting and maintaining appropriate access under park rules.
firefly-light.expectedEvidence: Trace artificial light to interference with the animals' communication and explain a cause-matched response. Compare the three supplied priorities, state what is still unknown and justify a design choice without a zero-impact guarantee.
firefly-light.nearMiss: Claims a flower bed fixes light disturbance or that any conservation benefit proves all visitor/safety requirements can be ignored.
firefly-light.changedCase: Move the proposal to daytime away from firefly display habitat: revise the light-specific conclusion rather than copy the earlier risk claim.

ship-sound.sourceSummary: DFO describes large-vessel propeller sound overlapping signals important to marine animals and context-dependent masking/behavioural effects.
ship-sound.attributionLimits: No figure or local sound measurement is claimed. Original transport/conservation perspectives are not authentic testimony or a finding about a named vessel.
ship-sound.question: Original brief: a ferry planner values a reliable connection, a conservation worker wants animal signals detectable and a coastal resident values both transport and marine life. Given the DFO summaries, assess a proposed noisy route through a supplied animal communication/feeding area. Compare investigating route, timing and noise-reduction options while checking whether the transport purpose remains met.
ship-sound.expectedEvidence: Explain sound masking as interference with detecting an important signal, rather than noise literally stopping all sound travel. Compare priorities, identify evidence needed about species/exposure and justify a bounded response; acknowledge uncertainty and transport needs.
ship-sound.nearMiss: Says all ocean sound is harmful, all ships cause the same effect or reducing one source proves every animal population has recovered.
ship-sound.changedCase: The revised route has less overlap with the supplied animals' signal use but longer travel: weigh the changed conditions and ask for actual noise/fuel/habitat information rather than declare the longer route automatically greener.

wholeClaimReview.readScope: Complete three contributor cards, ZL9 and insect-conservation pedagogy/learn/assess/sources/provenance read; cOJ has no saved guide. All 14 direct/transitive hard-closure cards and 11 hard edges read. No fresh blanket verification of inherited guide citations.
componentBoundaries: ZL9 supplies device/signalling knowledge. These impact tasks do not replace its whole physical design/build/test/improve with agreed code and distance comparison. If assessing the whole claim, build two safe indoor light/string devices, test actual reception and improve; no road trial.
Insect conservation supplies the light-threat mechanism; its other threats, pollination/food and realistic actions remain whole-claim requirements. It is not a marine-noise topic.

cOJ supplies the actual competing-factor ranking/justification operation across the prepared briefs; no saved guide or older-topic scope is changed. Marine evidence comes from the source/task, not an insect score.
wholeClaimReview.hardReadiness: Existing light/sound vocabulary and insect/ecosystem paths remain intact. Source-task performance is not automatic whole-claim or prerequisite mastery.

safety: Source-based classroom comparisons, not road-crossing, hearing tests, medical fitting, bright/noisy field disturbance or animal handling. Fictional perspectives require no personal health disclosure. Any separate device build uses adult-approved low light and comfortable sound indoors.
